faqs.q: What standard governs a roof thermal imaging inspection in East Orange?

c.v: ASTM C1153, the Standard Practice for Location of Wet Insulation in Roofing Systems Using Infrared Imaging, governs a roof thermal imaging inspection and ranks as the most commonly used infrared roof moisture standard, per ASTM and the NRCA.

runs.v: ASTM C1153 requires verification of every suspected wet area by core cut, probe, or calibrated moisture meter.

faqs.q: Why does thermal imaging suit East Orange apartment and walk-up roofs?

runs.v: Thermal imaging suits East Orange's apartment and walk-up stock because it reads the roof from above without entering the occupied units below, where interior access follows New Jersey landlord-tenant notice, per IIBEC. Moisture-trapped insulation holds a higher heat capacity and cools more slowly than dry insulation, so after sunset the wet area reads as a warm anomaly that a camera resolving roughly 0.2°F picks up, per Fluke and IIBEC.

faqs.q: Can a thermal imaging inspection be done during the day in East Orange?

runs.v: A thermal imaging inspection scans after sunset, because ASTM C1153 sets optimal conditions of a clear sunny day followed by a clear night, when the dry roof releases heat fast and the wet area holds a sharp warm contrast. Winter narrows the contrast to roughly 5°F against roughly 20°F in summer, per ASTM C1153 via IIBEC and Fluke.

faqs.q: Does a thermal imaging inspection in East Orange require a permit, and what about historic buildings?

runs.v: No. A thermal imaging inspection documents condition rather than triggering a permit; the repair that follows needs one on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building only when it covers more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, filed through the East Orange Building Division at the Department of Property Maintenance, 44 City Hall Plaza. National Register listing alone places no restriction on a privately funded reroof, per the National Park Service, but confirm current local requirements with the East Orange Department of Planning, Policy & Development.

faqs.q: Does thermal imaging find the exact leak entry point in an East Orange apartment building?

runs.v: No. An infrared camera detects the wet insulation a roof leak leaves behind rather than the entry point itself, because the wet-insulation footprint sits displaced from the breach and the camera reads temperature patterns rather than water, per Fluke, IIBEC, and the NRCA. A core cut, probe, or calibrated moisture meter confirms each anomaly under ASTM C1153; finding the breach takes a separate check of the flashings, seams, and penetrations upslope of the wet area.
